_stepFormat: steps are 0-based pitch classes within one equave of that EDO, relative to the scale ROOT (root=0)
quantized12Rule: for any EDO without a native 12-EDO category: steps = sort(dedupe(round(cents*EDO/1200) % EDO)); Chromatic (null cents) = all EDO steps; drop the result if identical to an existing native scale of that EDO

Solaris.description: Mode 1 (bright, starts on L). Cmaj7 below, D major triad above. The brightest mode — major 7th arpeggio grounding a shifted major triad.

Lunaris.description: Mode 2 (reflective, starts on s). Cm7 below, Db major above. Minor seventh chord grounding a chromatic-root major triad.

Stellaris.description: Mode 3 (bright variant, starts on L). Cmaj7 below, Dm above. Like Solaris but the upper triad turns minor.

Umbra.description: Mode 4 (dark, starts on s). Cm7 below, Db major above (rooted a semitone up). The darkest pairing — minor seventh plus Neapolitan.

Aurea.description: Mode 5 (golden, starts on L). C7 (dominant) below, Dm above. The Hendrix mode — dominant seventh chord against a minor triad.

Cava.description: Mode 6 (hollow, starts on s). Cø (half-dim) below, Db major above. Tension and darkness — the diminished fifth in the lower tetrachord.

Libra.description: Mode 7 (balanced, palindromic). Cm7 below, Dm above. Palindromic step pattern (3,4,3,4,3,4,3) — the 'Dorian' of the hyperdiatonic, most balanced mode.

Hyperdiatonic.description: ME(13,24). The unique 13-note two-octave scale with all diatonic structural properties. Lower octave: C Db Eb F G A B. Upper octave: C D E F# G# A#. Contains all 12 pitch classes distributed across registers. Generated by minor ninths (13 semitones). Step pattern: 1 2 2 2 2 2 1 2 2 2 2 2 2.

Hyperdiatonic Complement.description: ME(11,24). The complement of the hyperdiatonic — analogous to the pentatonic's relationship to the diatonic. 11 notes, step pattern (2 2 2 2 2 3 2 2 2 2 3). Also WF, ME, MP, and deep.

Major-Minor Split.description: C major below, C natural minor above. The Persichetti classic — bright foundation, dark upper register.

Mixolydian-Phrygian Split.description: Maximum brightness contrast. Dominant character below, Spanish color above.

Melodic Minor (Traditional).description: The original multi-octave scale — major 6th and 7th ascending, minor descending. Finally representable as a single scale object.

Harmonic Minor-Lydian Split.description: Tension below (augmented 2nd), openness above (#4). Bartók territory.

Blues-Dorian Expansion.description: Hexatonic blues below, full Dorian above. The upper octave gives you more color notes for soloing.

Thai Classical (7-TET).description: The Thai 7-tone equal scale mapped to even steps of 14-EDO. Every interval is ~171¢ — no major/minor distinction. Thai classical instruments (ranat, khong wong) are tuned to this near-equal system. The sound is immediately recognizable and quite unlike any Western scale.

Thai Pentatonic.description: Five-note Thai mode — the most common subset used in folk melodies. Steps of 2, 2, 4, 2, 4 (in 14-EDO).

Hirajoshi.description: The 'civilian scale.' Steps of 3,2,5,2,5 in 17-EDO. The narrow semitone (step size 2 = 141¢) is wider than 12-EDO's 100¢, matching the shakuhachi's characteristic pitch bending range.

Insen.description: The scale of the shakuhachi master Kinko Kurosawa. The opening minor second (141¢) is a distinctive Japanese interval — wider and more 'singing' than 12-EDO.

Miyako-bushi (In scale).description: The urban mode — associated with koto and shamisen in Edo-period music. The wide fourth at step 7 (494¢) is characteristic.

Yo scale.description: The folk/rural mode. Pentatonic without semitones — all steps are 2 or 3 (141¢ or 212¢). The backbone of min'yo folk singing.

Ryukyu.description: Okinawan scale. Major character with a distinctive sharp 4th and sharp 7th. The sound of sanshin and Okinawan folk music.

Hyper-Ionian.description: Mode 1 (6,5,6,5,6,5,5). Lower: R m3+ P5 M7. Upper: m2+ P4+ M6. 19-EDO's meantone character makes the lower arpeggio a lush major 7th.

Hyper-Dorian.description: Mode 2 (5,6,5,6,5,5,6). Minor character below, contrasting upper register.

Hyper-Phrygian.description: Mode 3 (6,5,6,5,5,6,5). Like Ionian below but the upper register shifts.

Hyper-Lydian.description: Mode 4 (5,6,5,5,6,5,6). Dark below, chromatic tension with the b2 above.

Hyper-Mixolydian.description: Mode 5 (6,5,5,6,5,6,5). Dominant seventh feel below — the m7 in the lower arpeggio.

Hyper-Aeolian.description: Mode 6 (5,5,6,5,6,5,6). Darkest mode — tritone in the lower octave.

Hyper-Locrian.description: Mode 7 (5,6,5,6,5,6,5). Palindromic — the balanced 'Dorian' of the hyperdiatonic.

Solaris.description: Mode 1. Lower octave: R SM3 P5 SM7. Upper: M2 v5 SM6. Supermajor seventh arpeggio below, contrasting tritone color above.

Lunaris.description: Mode 2. Lower octave: R sm3 P5 sm7. Upper: M2 P4 ^5. Minor character below, quartal character above.

Stellaris.description: Mode 3. Lower octave: R SM3 P5 SM7. Upper: M2 P4 SM6. Like Mode 1 below but with a fourth replacing the tritone above.

Umbra.description: Mode 4. Lower octave: R sm3 P5 sm7. Upper: vm2 P4 ^5. Dark below, chromatic tension on the vm2 above.

Aurea.description: Mode 5. Lower octave: R SM3 P5 sm7. Upper: M2 P4 SM6. Dominant seventh feel below, open fourths above.

Cava.description: Mode 6. Lower octave: R sm3 ^4 sm7. Upper: vm2 P4 ^5. The darkest mode — tritone in the lower tetrachord.

Libra.description: Mode 7. Symmetrical step pattern (5,8,5,8,5,8,5). Lower: R sm3 P5 sm7. Upper: M2 P4 SM6.

Solaris.description: Mode 1 (3,5,5,3,5,5,3,5,5,5). Lower: R n2 SM3 P5 sm7 SM7. Upper: M2 sm3 v5 SM6. Six notes below, four above. The lower octave outlines a rich harmonic field; the upper thins out.

Aequa.description: Mode 2 (5,5,3,5,5,3,5,5,5,3). Five notes per octave — the most balanced distribution. Pentatonic density in both registers.

Lunaris.description: Mode 3 (5,3,5,5,3,5,5,5,3,5). Six below, four above. Minor quality opening.

Nebula.description: Mode 4 (3,5,5,3,5,5,5,3,5,5). Same lower octave content as Mode 1 but upper octave shifts — the tritone (v5) moves to P4.

Gemina.description: Mode 5 (5,5,3,5,5,5,3,5,5,3). Balanced 5+5. The small step cluster shifts upward.

Vela.description: Mode 6 (5,3,5,5,5,3,5,5,3,5). Five per octave. Three consecutive large steps create a wide gap in the lower register.

Umbra.description: Mode 7 (3,5,5,5,3,5,5,3,5,5). Dense lower octave with chromatic opening (n2).

Aurea.description: Mode 8 (5,5,5,3,5,5,3,5,5,3). Balanced. Three large steps at the bottom create a wide-open foundation.

Libra.description: Mode 9 (5,5,3,5,5,3,5,5,3,5). Palindromic — the 'Dorian' of the 10-note hyperdiatonic. Most balanced and symmetrical.

Bilawal (Major).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni. The natural major scale. Uses 5/4 major third and 5/3 major sixth.

Yaman / Kalyan.description: Sa Re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Tivra (sharp) Ma gives Lydian character. The quintessential evening raga — serene, devotional. 22-EDO's tivra Ma at 600¢ (≈7/5) is more septimal than 12-EDO's tritone.

Bhairavi.description: Sa re ga Ma Pa dha ni. All komal (flat) except Sa, Ma, Pa. The 'queen of ragas' — morning devotional, deeply emotional. Komal Ga at step 6 (327¢ ≈ 6/5) is the classical minor third.

Bhairav.description: Sa re Ga Ma Pa dha Ni. Flat 2nd and 6th, natural 3rd and 7th. The augmented-second leaps (re→Ga, dha→Ni) give Bhairav its intense, solemn dawn character.

Kafi (Dorian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Komal Ga and Ni. Romantic, playful, associated with spring and Holi. The classical minor third at step 6 distinguishes this from the septimal Darbari.

Khamaj (Mixolydian).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Natural everything except komal Ni. Light, romantic, late evening. The flat seventh at step 19 (≈ 9/5) gives a sweet dominant quality.

Asavari (Aeolian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Natural minor equivalent. Pathos and devotion.

Todi.description: Sa re ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Extremely dark — flat 2nd, flat 3rd, sharp 4th, flat 6th. One of the most chromatic and intense ragas. Morning raga of deep gravity.

Darbari Kanada.description: Sa Re ga↓ Ma Pa dha↓ ni. THE raga that proves why 22-EDO matters for Indian music. Darbari's komal Ga is specifically the LOWER septimal minor third (step 5 = 273¢ ≈ 7/6), not the classical minor third (step 6 ≈ 6/5). Similarly dha↓ at step 14 (≈ 14/9). In 12-EDO these collapse to the same notes as Kafi — in 22-EDO you hear the difference that defines Darbari's gravity and majesty.

Marwa.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Traditionally Pa is omitted or touched lightly. Komal Re with tivra Ma creates extreme tension. Late afternoon raga of restless longing.

Puriya.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Same notes as Marwa but different melodic treatment — Pa is completely avoided in Puriya. Sunset raga.

Malkauns.description: Sa ga Ma dha ni. Pentatonic, all komal except Sa and Ma. Midnight raga — deep, meditative, powerful. The absence of Re, Ga shuddh, Pa, and Dha creates a stark, haunting sound.

Bhupali / Bhoop.description: Sa Re Ga Pa Dha. Major pentatonic. Evening raga — pure, sweet, simple. No Ma or Ni gives it an open, floating quality.

Desh.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Same as Khamaj but with distinct melodic grammar. The raga of patriotism and monsoon. Komal Ni in descent gives a characteristic 'sigh.'

Durga.description: Sa Re Ma Pa Dha. Pentatonic — no Ga or Ni. Serene, devotional, evening. The missing third gives it ambiguity between major and minor.

Bageshri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Same notes as Kafi but with different emphasis and melodic movement. Midnight raga — romantic yearning.

Jaunpuri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Same notes as Asavari but treated as a morning raga with distinct phrases. The komal Dha at step 15 (≈ 8/5) is characteristic.

Miyan ki Malhar.description: Sa Re ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha ni. Uses BOTH natural and sharp Ma — 8 notes. The monsoon raga, evoking rain and clouds. The Ma/Ma# oscillation is its signature.

Shree.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Tivra Ma with komal Re and komal Dha. Serious, majestic evening raga. The augmented intervals create grandeur.

Bihag.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Uses both Ma shuddh and tivra — 8 notes. Late night romantic raga. The Ma/Ma# interplay creates a shimmering, yearning quality.

Shankarabharanam (Major).description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3. The 29th Melakarta — equivalent to Western major scale. Foundation of Carnatic music theory.

Kalyani.description: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3. The 65th Melakarta — equivalent to Lydian/Yaman.

Kharaharapriya.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2. The 22nd Melakarta — Dorian character. One of the most performed Carnatic ragas.

Todi (Carnatic).description: S R1 G2 M2 P D1 N3. The 8th Melakarta — Carnatic Todi differs slightly from Hindustani Todi in melodic treatment.

Mayamalavagowla.description: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3. The 15th Melakarta — equivalent to Bhairav. The first raga taught to Carnatic students. Double augmented seconds.

Hanumatodi.description: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2. The 8th Melakarta with shuddh Ma — Phrygian character.

Harikambhoji.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2. The 28th Melakarta — Mixolydian character.

Natabhairavi.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2. The 20th Melakarta — natural minor.

Charukeshi.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D1 N2. The 26th Melakarta — major scale with flat 6th and 7th. Bittersweet character.

Simhendramadhyamam.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N3. The 57th Melakarta — harmonic minor equivalent. The raised Ni creates a leading tone within a minor framework.

Hirajoshi.description: In 22-EDO the semitone steps (1 step = 55¢) are narrower than in 12-EDO, intensifying the characteristic tension. The wide gaps (8 steps = 436¢ ≈ 9/7) add a septimal dimension absent in the standard version.

Insen.description: The narrow 2nd (step 2, 109¢) captures the shakuhachi's microtonal approach note. The 7/6 third (step 5, 273¢) adds depth.

Miyako-bushi.description: The koto scale. The wide fourth (step 9, 491¢) and chromatic cluster at the fifth (steps 13-14) define its character.

Kumoi.description: The 'cloudy' scale — wide 2nd, natural 4th, major 6th. Associated with court music (gagaku). 22-EDO's septimal intervals give it an ancient quality.

Neutral Hyper-Ionian.description: Stacked neutral thirds below (R, n3, n6, n9). Upper octave fills the gaps. Nearly equidistant — the 24-EDO hyperdiatonic is the most 'even' of all, reflecting 24-EDO's neutral character.

Neutral Hyper-Dorian.description: Mode 2. The small step (6) falls between octaves, subtly compressing the upper register.

Neutral Hyper-Phrygian.description: Mode 3. The small step falls at the octave boundary — the lower octave is slightly compressed.

Neutral Hyper-Lydian.description: Mode 4. Small step at the bottom — the lowest interval is a quarter-tone narrower than the rest.

Neutral Hyper-Mixolydian.description: Mode 5. Same pitch content as Ionian but different starting point in the chain.

Neutral Hyper-Aeolian.description: Mode 6. The near-equidistance means modes are very similar — the character shifts are subtle.

Neutral Hyper-Locrian.description: Mode 7. In 24-EDO, the hyperdiatonic modes are nearly indistinguishable due to the quasi-equal step pattern.

Rast-Bayati Split.description: Rast (bright, major-ish) below, Bayati (plaintive, neutral 2nd) above. The most fundamental maqam contrast.

Ajam-Hicaz Split.description: Pure major below, augmented-2nd Hicaz above. Western brightness dissolving into Ottoman drama.

Bayati-Rast Ascent.description: Dark Bayati below opening into bright Rast above. A sunrise — common in actual maqam performance practice where the upper jins differs from the lower.

Sikah-Kurd Split.description: Sikah (neutral thirds throughout) below, Kurd (Phrygian-like) above. Floating neutrality grounded by minor gravity.

H\u00fczzam-Nahawand Split.description: Restless Hüzzam below, settled Nahawand (minor) above. Tension resolving into familiarity as you ascend.

Saba Expansion.description: Saba's broken tetrachord below (the compressed 4th), Rast's full brightness above. The lower register is constrained and yearning; the upper register opens up and breathes.

Hyperdiatonic.description: ME(25,48). The 24-EDO hyperdiatonic: 25 notes across two octaves. Lower octave: 13 notes (quarter-tone + 12 semitones). Upper octave: 12 notes (all semitones). Contains all 24 pitch classes. Generator = 25 quarter-tones (minor ninth + quarter-tone). Step pattern: (1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2).

Hyperdiatonic Complement.description: ME(23,48). Complement of the 24-EDO hyperdiatonic. 23 notes, step pattern (2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 3 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 3). Also WF, ME, MP, and deep.

Slendro (5-EDO approx).description: The older gamelan scale. Five near-equal steps. In 24-EDO: steps of 250, 250, 200, 250, 250 cents — close to 5-EDO's 240¢. The slight unevenness actually matches real gamelan tuning better than pure 5-EDO.

Pelog Nem.description: Seven-note pelog with pathet Nem emphasis (notes 2, 3, 5, 6 prominent). Steps alternate ~100¢ and ~200¢, approximating 9-EDO subsets. This is the most common pelog mode.

Pelog Lima.description: Same pitches as Nem but different melodic emphasis and hierarchy. Notes 1, 2, 4, 5 are primary.

Pelog Barang.description: Pelog mode emphasizing the upper tetrachord. Wider opening interval gives a brighter character.

Degung (Sundanese).description: Five-note Sundanese pelog scale. The wide gap (6→14, 667¢) is characteristic of Sundanese gamelan's more ethereal sound compared to Central Javanese.

Shur.description: The foundational Persian dastgah. The 3rd degree at step 5 (250¢) is a koron — between Eb and E, a neutral interval that defines the Persian sound. Shur is melancholy, introspective.

Segah.description: Starts on the segah tone (neutral third). Mystical, Sufi-associated. The opening neutral second (150¢) is the sori modifier.

Chahargah.description: The 'four-note' dastgah. More chromatic and dramatic than Shur. The augmented second (8→10, 100¢ then 10→14, 200¢) gives it intensity.

Mahur.description: The closest to a Western major scale but with Persian phrasing and ornamental tradition. Bright, festive.

Homayun.description: A derivative of Shur with an augmented second. Deeply melancholic — associated with grief and loss in Persian culture.

Nava.description: Uses neutral intervals (steps 7 and 21 at 350¢ and 1050¢). A transitional dastgah with modal modulation built into its structure.

Afshari.description: A Shur derivative emphasizing the upper tetrachord. Pastoral, associated with folk music of the Afshar tribe.

Bayat-e Tork.description: Bright and lively, associated with Turkic-influenced Persian music. The semitone clusters (4-5, 18-19) give it a distinctive sparkle.

Hyper-Ionian.description: Mode 1 (6,11,6,11,6,11,11). Generated by the subfifth (658¢), not the true meantone fifth. Lower: R sm3 P4+ SM6. This has a distinctly non-diatonic character — subminor thirds and wide fourths.

Hyper-Dorian.description: Mode 2 (11,6,11,6,11,11,6). Wide steps dominate — the 11-step intervals (~426¢) are supermajor thirds.

Hyper-Aeolian.description: Mode 6 (11,11,6,11,6,11,6). Darkest — two wide steps at the bottom.

Kartli-Kakheti Mode.description: Seven roughly equal steps subdividing 1060¢ (~quintave + wide octave). The Eastern Georgian mode — near-equal tetrachords. Each step ~176¢, close to 7-TET. The characteristic wide octave at step 34 (1200¢) is slightly sharp of pure.

Svaneti Trichordal.description: Six-note scale built from two trichords separated by a whole tone. Svanetian polyphony uses the narrowest melodic range of any Georgian tradition — often within a fifth.

Georgian Quintave Tetrachord.description: The fundamental Georgian unit: the fifth (20 steps = 706¢) divided into four unequal steps (small neutral 2nd, large neutral 2nd, whole tone, large neutral 2nd). This is the building block of Georgian polyphony.

Georgian Church Mode (Erkvanidze).description: Erkvanidze's model of the Georgian liturgical scale. The 4th degree at step 14 (494¢) is slightly flat of pure 4/3, characteristic of the tradition. The neutral seconds give Georgian church singing its otherworldly quality.

Gurian Dance Mode.description: Western Georgian (Gurian) mode with wider whole-tone steps. Gurian music is the most rhythmically complex Georgian tradition, with krimanchuli yodeling.

Hyper-Ionian.description: Mode 1 (10,13,10,13,10,13,13). Generated by the down-fifth (673¢). Lower: R m3 v5 vm7. Upper: sm3 ^M3 SM6. Stacked minor thirds below, septimal color above.

Hyper-Dorian.description: Mode 2 (13,10,13,10,13,13,10). Wide steps lead — downmajor thirds (380¢) alternate with minor thirds.

Hyper-Mixolydian.description: Mode 5 (10,13,13,10,13,10,13). The small-step pair shifts — tritone-ish span in lower octave.

Hyper-Aeolian.description: Mode 6 (13,13,10,13,10,13,10). Two wide steps at bottom — darkest mode.

Hyper-Ionian.description: Mode 1 (18,13,18,13,18,13,13). Near-JI fifth generator. Lower: R M3+ P5 ~M7. 53-EDO's legendary JI accuracy means the lower arpeggio is practically a just major seventh chord.

Hyper-Mixolydian.description: Mode 5 (18,13,13,18,13,18,13). Dominant — the lower arpeggio includes a minor 7th.

Hyper-Aeolian.description: Mode 6 (13,13,18,13,18,13,18). Darkest — tritone in the lower tetrachord.

Bilawal (Major).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni. Pure 5-limit JI major scale. 53-EDO renders every interval within 1¢ of just.

Yaman / Kalyan.description: Sa Re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Tivra Ma at 7/5 (step 26). The evening raga of serenity. In 53-EDO the Ma# is distinctly septimal — purer than any 12-EDO tritone.

Bhairavi.description: Sa re ga Ma Pa dha ni. All komal. The queen of ragas. Every interval is near-just: komal Re = 16/15, komal Ga = 6/5, komal Dha = 8/5, komal Ni = 9/5.

Bhairav.description: Sa re Ga Ma Pa dha Ni. The augmented seconds (re→Ga = 274¢, dha→Ni = 274¢) are near-just 7/6 intervals. Dawn raga of solemn intensity.

Kafi (Dorian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Komal Ga at 6/5 (step 14) and komal Ni at 9/5 (step 45). Playful, romantic.

Khamaj (Mixolydian).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Natural everything except komal Ni. Late evening romance.

Asavari (Aeolian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Natural minor with just 6/5 minor third and 8/5 minor sixth.

Todi.description: Sa re ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. The darkest of the major ragas. Komal Re (16/15), komal Ga (6/5), tivra Ma (7/5), komal Dha (8/5) — maximum chromatic tension with just intervals.

Darbari Kanada.description: Sa Re ga↓ Ma Pa dha↓ ni. 53-EDO's crown jewel for Indian music. The septimal komal Ga at step 12 (≈7/6, 272¢) and septimal Dha at step 34 (≈14/9, 770¢) are clearly distinct from the classical komal positions (steps 14 and 36). This is the microtonal distinction that defines Darbari's gravity — impossible in 12-EDO, approximate in 22-EDO, near-perfect in 53-EDO.

Marwa.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Traditionally Pa is barely touched. The komal Re against shuddh Ga creates a wide 281¢ leap (≈7/6). Restless sunset raga.

Puriya.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Dha Ni. Pa omitted entirely. Six-note scale of intense longing. The absence of the fifth creates harmonic suspension.

Malkauns.description: Sa ga Ma dha ni. Pentatonic, all komal. Midnight raga of depth. Pure 6/5 minor third and 8/5 minor sixth in near-just intonation.

Bhupali / Bhoop.description: Sa Re Ga Pa Dha. Major pentatonic with just 5/4 third and 5/3 sixth. Pure, sweet evening raga.

Desh.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Monsoon raga. Same notes as Khamaj but distinct melodic grammar — the komal Ni appears mainly in descent.

Durga.description: Sa Re Ma Pa Dha. Pentatonic without Ga or Ni — ambiguous between major and minor. Serene devotion.

Bageshri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Same notes as Kafi, different soul. Midnight raga of romantic yearning. The Dha (5/3) against ni (9/5) creates a just 27/25 whole tone.

Miyan ki Malhar.description: Sa Re ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha ni. Eight notes — both Ma positions. The monsoon raga. The oscillation between Ma (4/3) and Ma# (7/5) is its heartbeat.

Shree.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Majestic evening raga. The re→Ga leap (272¢ ≈ 7/6) and dha→Ni leap (272¢) give it grandeur.

Bihag.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Eight notes with both Ma. Late night romance. In 53-EDO the Ma/Ma# distinction (4/3 vs 7/5) is crystal clear.

Poorvi.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Same notes as Shree but different treatment. Sunset raga — the komal Re and komal Dha against natural Ga and Ni create exotic augmented intervals.

Jaunpuri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Morning raga with Asavari's notes but distinct phrases. The komal Dha (8/5) is characteristic.

Shankarabharanam.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3. 29th Melakarta. Pure 5-limit major. The foundation.

Kalyani.description: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3. 65th Melakarta. Lydian character with septimal Ma#.

Kharaharapriya.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2. 22nd Melakarta. Dorian — one of the most performed Carnatic ragas.

Todi (Carnatic).description: S R1 G2 M2 P D1 N3. 8th Melakarta.

Mayamalavagowla.description: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3. 15th Melakarta. Bhairav equivalent. The first raga Carnatic students learn. Double augmented seconds rendered in near-just intonation.

Hanumatodi.description: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2. Phrygian character with just minor intervals.

Harikambhoji.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2. 28th Melakarta. Mixolydian.

Natabhairavi.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2. 20th Melakarta. Natural minor.

Charukeshi.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D1 N2. 26th Melakarta. Major with flat 6th and 7th.

Simhendramadhyamam.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N3. 57th Melakarta. Harmonic minor with just intervals.

Mechakalyani.description: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N2. 65th Melakarta variant. Lydian dominant — tivra Ma with komal Ni.

Hemavati.description: S R2 G2 M2 P D2 N2. 58th Melakarta. Dorian #4 — the komal Ga with tivra Ma creates a tritone span.

Shur.description: Shur in near-just intonation. The koron at step 13 (294¢, between 6/5 and 7/6) captures the specific Persian neutral quality that 24-EDO approximates but 53-EDO nails.

Segah.description: The sori opening (step 8, 181¢ ≈ 10/9) is precise in 53-EDO.

Chahargah.description: The augmented second (steps 17→22, 113¢) is close to 16/15 — pure in 53-EDO.

Homayun.description: The wide leap from koron Re to shuddh Ga (steps 5→17, 272¢ ≈ 7/6) gives Homayun its characteristic ache.

Bilawal (Major).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni. Pure JI major in 72-EDO — identical to your existing JI Major scale. Every interval within 5¢ of just.

Yaman / Kalyan.description: Sa Re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Tivra Ma at step 35 (≈7/5, exact within 0.3¢). The serene evening raga with a septimally pure augmented fourth.

Bhairavi.description: Sa re ga Ma Pa dha ni. All komal. Komal Re at 16/15 (step 7), komal Ga at 6/5 (step 19). The queen of ragas in near-perfect JI.

Bhairav.description: Sa re Ga Ma Pa dha Ni. The augmented seconds (re→Ga and dha→Ni) span 267¢ and 267¢ — almost exactly 7/6. Dawn solemnity.

Kafi (Dorian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Komal Ga at step 19 (≈6/5) distinguishes this from Darbari's step 16 (≈7/6). Romantic spring raga.

Khamaj (Mixolydian).description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Natural everything except komal Ni at 9/5. Sweet late evening.

Asavari (Aeolian).description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Just natural minor. Pure 6/5 third and 8/5 sixth.

Todi.description: Sa re ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Maximum darkness. The tivra Ma at exactly 7/5 against komal Ga at 6/5 creates a septimal tritone of extraordinary purity.

Darbari Kanada.description: Sa Re ga↓ Ma Pa dha↓ ni. 72-EDO's finest achievement for Indian music. The septimal komal Ga at step 16 (267¢ ≈ 7/6, error 0.2¢) is practically exact JI. The septimal komal Dha at step 46 (767¢ ≈ 14/9, error 1.6¢) is equally precise. Compare: step 16 vs step 19 (komal Ga in Kafi) = 50¢ difference. This is the gap that defines Darbari — clearly audible, precisely tuned.

Marwa.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Pa barely touched. The re→Ga leap (267¢ ≈ 7/6) launches into the luminous 5/4 third. Restless sunset.

Puriya.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Dha Ni. Pa omitted. Six notes of intense longing.

Malkauns.description: Sa ga Ma dha ni. Pentatonic, all komal. Midnight depth with just 6/5 and 8/5.

Bhupali / Bhoop.description: Sa Re Ga Pa Dha. Major pentatonic in near-just intonation.

Desh.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Monsoon raga.

Durga.description: Sa Re Ma Pa Dha. The ambiguous pentatonic — no third, no seventh.

Bageshri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa Dha ni. Midnight romance.

Miyan ki Malhar.description: Sa Re ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha ni. Eight notes. The Ma/Ma# oscillation (4/3 ↔ 7/5, steps 30 ↔ 35) is the sound of rain.

Shree.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Majestic evening grandeur.

Bihag.description: Sa Re Ga Ma Ma# Pa Dha Ni. Eight notes. Late night shimmer.

Poorvi.description: Sa re Ga Ma# Pa dha Ni. Sunset intensity.

Jaunpuri.description: Sa Re ga Ma Pa dha ni. Morning Asavari variant.

Darbari Kanada (extended).description: Sa Re ga↓ ga Ma Pa dha↓ dha ni. Nine notes — includes BOTH septimal and classical komal Ga and Dha. In performance, Darbari oscillates between ga↓ (step 16, 7/6) and ga (step 19, 6/5). 72-EDO is the only standard EDO that captures both positions distinctly. This is how a master sitarist actually plays Darbari.

Shankarabharanam.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3. 29th Melakarta. Pure JI major.

Kalyani.description: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3. 65th Melakarta.

Kharaharapriya.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2. 22nd Melakarta. Dorian.

Todi (Carnatic).description: S R1 G2 M2 P D1 N3. 8th Melakarta.

Mayamalavagowla.description: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3. 15th Melakarta. First raga taught. Double augmented seconds in near-just tuning.

Hanumatodi.description: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2. Phrygian.

Harikambhoji.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2. 28th Melakarta. Mixolydian.

Natabhairavi.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2. 20th Melakarta. Natural minor.

Charukeshi.description: S R2 G3 M1 P D1 N2. 26th Melakarta.

Simhendramadhyamam.description: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N3. 57th Melakarta. Harmonic minor.

Mechakalyani.description: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N2. Lydian dominant.

Hemavati.description: S R2 G2 M2 P D2 N2. 58th Melakarta. Dorian #4.

Ramapriya.description: S R1 G3 M2 P D1 N3. 52nd Melakarta. Bhairav with tivra Ma — an exotic combination of flat 2nd, pure major 3rd, septimal tritone, flat 6th, and major 7th.

Vakulabharanam.description: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N2. 14th Melakarta. Bhairav with komal Ni instead of shuddh.

Slendro (JI Harrison).description: Lou Harrison's just intonation slendro: 1/1, 8/7, 4/3 (approx), 3/2, 7/4 (approx). Harrison dedicated much of his career to bridging gamelan and Western composition.

Slendro (5-EDO).description: Pure 5-EDO approximation in 72-EDO (every ~14.4 steps). The idealized equal slendro.

Pelog (JI Harrison).description: Harrison's JI pelog: 1/1, 16/15, 8/7, 4/3, 3/2, 8/5, 7/4. Bridges gamelan and Western tuning theory.

Pelog (9-EDO approx).description: 9-EDO subset in 72-EDO. Seven equal 133¢ steps. The idealized pelog grid — real gamelans deviate from this but it captures the framework.
